title: docs(schema-reference): ObjectGridSchema.sort row reads SortConfig[] only (objectui#10581)
body:
Fixes #10581

Clause-②: no

`Clause-②: no` — reference docs stop teaching a refused spelling; no code, export or accept set moves.

## What changed

One row of `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, in the `ObjectGridSchema` property table:

- before: `sort` | `string \| SortConfig[]` | "Default sort configuration."
- after: `sort` | `SortConfig[]` | "Default sort configuration. The string clause (`"name desc"`) was retired in objectui#8221 and now fails validation."

Docs only, under `content/` (not a workspace package, not released): no changeset. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` agrees (verdict line below).

## The retired-row form, and where it was copied from

The row copies the form the same file already uses for a live key whose value lost a member: the `CalendarViewSchema` table's `view` row, which keeps its row, narrows the Type column to what survives, and says "`"agenda"` was retired in objectui#5740 and now fails validation." The Type-column `*retired*` / `RETIRED` form (the `BaseSchema` `body` row, the `related` row) is for a retired KEY; `sort` is live, so that form does not apply.

## Premise check (objectui `origin/main` at `6c2f3c533`)

- The row read `string \| SortConfig[]`, as the card said.
- `@object-ui/types` declares `ObjectGridSchema.sort` as `SortConfig[]` on the TypeScript face and as `z.array(SortConfigSchema)` on the zod mirror (describe text: "array only; the legacy string clause is retired — objectui#8221").
- The grid refuses a string at runtime: the `typeof schemaSort === 'string'` arm in `ObjectGrid.tsx` ("the legacy string `sort` clause is RETIRED (objectui#8221, decision batch #77) and is REFUSED here rather than lowered") sends no `$orderby`, and `convertSortToQueryParams` reports the spelling once with `console.error`.
- "now fails validation" is an existing pin, not prose: `packages/types/src/__tests__/sort-string-arm-retired-8221.test.ts`, test "object-grid refuses the legacy string clause", asserts `ObjectGridSchema.safeParse` fails on `sort: 'name desc'` with an issue at path `sort`. It ran green at this head (below).

## Sweep of `content/`

No other row or example in `content/` authors a string `sort` on a grid-family node. Searches run: quoted `field asc|desc` clauses; `sort:` / `"sort":` followed by a string or a string array; every `sort` table row. What they found:

- the `ObjectGridSchema` example in this file already writes `"sort": [{ "field": "name", "order": "asc" }]`;
- `plugin-grid.mdx`, `plugin-map.mdx`, `plugin-gantt.mdx` and `plugin-view.mdx` type or write `sort` as the array;
- the only string hits are not grid-family `sort`: `report-schema.mdx` `groupBy[].sort: 'asc'` (the report grouping direction enum), and the `$orderby` strings `'createdAt asc'` in `plugin-detail.mdx` and `'createdAt desc'` in `data-objectstack.mdx` (`DataSource.find` query params).

A repo-wide search for the union spelling `string | SortConfig` outside `content/` matches only changesets, a CHANGELOG and test comments that record the retirement.

## Gates (run locally at head `810b89da0`)

- `pnpm docs:check-links`, exit 0: "Links are valid across 17 scan roots."
- `pnpm check:doc-fences`, exit 0: "check:doc-fences — every TypeScript block in 227 document(s) is fenced ts/tsx/typescript …"
- `pnpm check:doc-example-ids`, exit 0: "414 real reference(s) all resolve in the catalog registry."
- `pnpm check:doc-types`, exit 0: "Every documented component type is registered."
- `node scripts/check-prompt-component-keys.mjs`, exit 0 (the same workflow as `check:doc-types`).
- `node scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs`, exit 0 (Build Docs job step; report-only census).
- `pnpm check:doc-example-readers`, exit 0; `pnpm check:spec-symbols`, exit 0: "nothing cites a key its spec symbol does not declare."
- `node scripts/check-shell-escape-residue.mjs`, exit 0; `pnpm check:docs-route-closure`, exit 0.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`, exit 0: "VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)".
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`, exit 0: "check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 8717 tracked text file(s) …)".
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, exit 0: "No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed." `check-changeset-claims`, exit 0 (report-only).
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`: "NOT GOVERNED".
- Tests that read this file: `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --changed` names it, and its ledger names 18 test files (the `content/docs/**` glob plus the two that read this file by name). Those 18 plus the objectui#8221 pin ran under the shared verify lock with `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: "Test Files 19 passed (19) · Tests 969 passed (969)", `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

No test pins this row's text (`Default sort configuration` has no hit outside the row), so no test changed.

## Acceptance notes

- No new pin was added, so there is no red-then-green pair to show. The "fails validation" claim rests on the existing objectui#8221 pin named above.
- Declared narrowing, left to CI: `check:doc-snippets` / Doc Snippet Types (it needs the packages' built `dist/*.d.ts` across a near-whole-workspace build closure). Its population is fenced ts/tsx blocks, and the edited row sits outside any fence (34 fence delimiters come before it, an even count), so this diff cannot move that gate's verdict. The Build Docs site build (`turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/site`) and the full test shards are also CI's. No workspace package is touched, so no package typecheck or test is owed.
- Observation only, not filed: the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` still declares `ObjectGridPropsSchema.sort` as `z.unknown()`, and it accepts `"name desc"` (measured with `safeParse`). objectstack `main` already declares it as `z.array(SortItemSchema)`, and its describe text refuses the string clause. The protocol face therefore catches up on the next spec release that objectui installs. This row documents the `@object-ui/types` face, which is the one this page covers.
